title: Fable 5 Takes the Math Crown, Cracking the Hardest Problem Yet - TCR 07/21/26
description:
Claude Fable 5 produced a 216-character counterexample disproving the 87-year-old Jacobian conjecture, AMD began shipping Helios as a rack-scale rival to Nvidia's 95% GPU grip with Microsoft deploying it across Azure, and a Nature Medicine trial gave four patients with complete spinal cord injury a median 13-point motor-score gain from stem-cell transplants with no tumors across 2-4 years.

https://sharedsapience.com/the-century-report-july-21-2026/

0:00 Open and framing
0:39 Claude Fable 5 ends an 87-year math conjecture
4:01 China's open weights split Washington's AI camp
8:09 The largest US copyright settlement clears
11:01 AMD's Helios rivals Nvidia with Microsoft aboard
14:22 Stem-cell therapy restores motor function after spinal injury
18:15 Close

This episode covers the Jacobian conjecture falling to Claude Fable 5 with GPT-5.6 proposing its replacement, Washington's AI advisers splitting into open war over China's free Kimi K3 open weights, Anthropic's $1.5 billion copyright settlement clearing final approval, AMD's Helios giving Nvidia a rack-scale rival with Microsoft aboard, and an iPSC-derived stem-cell therapy restoring motor function after complete cervical spinal cord injury.

The day's signal came from pure mathematics. Harvard's Levent Alpöge announced that Claude Fable 5 generated a 216-character object ending the Jacobian conjecture, open since 1939 and on Smale's list of the century's great problems, while GPT-5.6 proposed the refined conjecture to replace it. Set that beside a Nature Medicine trial where four men with complete cervical spinal cord injury regained measurable motor function, tumor-free across two to four years, and the shape of the week is clear: capabilities long filed under "unsolvable" are being reclassified as "not yet done." That compounding capability ran into the arrangements built to control it. AMD shipped Helios, a genuine rack-scale rival to Nvidia's near-total compute grip, with Microsoft, Meta, OpenAI, and Oracle aboard. Anthropic's $1.5 billion copyright settlement, the largest in US history, cleared final approval while leaving the training-data question unresolved. And Washington's AI advisers spent the weekend trading public insults over whether to fence out China's free Kimi K3 open weights, a fight whose stated safety rationale kept collapsing into a simpler commercial one.
